title: Parag Milk Foods to Invest ₹100 Crore, Quadruple Paneer Capacity to 80 Tonnes a Day
excerpt: The dairy maker will expand plants in Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh by June 2027, betting on the shift from unorganized to branded paneer. Paneer has grown 28% for the company in two years.
body:
• Parag Milk Foods will invest approximately ₹100 crore to expand its paneer manufacturing capacity from 20 metric tonnes per day to 80 MT per day, a four-fold increase.
  • The expansion covers facilities at Manchar in Maharashtra and Palamaner in Andhra Pradesh, mixing brownfield and greenfield projects, with commissioning expected by June 2027.
  • The investment will be funded through internal accruals, borrowings, or lease arrangements, and will produce both regular and high-protein paneer.
  • Paneer is a flagship category for the company, growing 28% over the last two years, with value-added products contributing more than 90% of turnover.

Parag Milk Foods said on Monday, September 21, that it plans to invest approximately ₹100 crore to expand its paneer manufacturing capacity to 80 metric tonnes per day from the existing 20 metric tonnes per day, quadrupling output at its facilities in Manchar, Maharashtra, and Palamaner, Andhra Pradesh. The expansion, planned for financial year 2027-28, is expected to be commissioned by June 2027.

The move addresses near-full utilization at the company's existing plants. Parag said the additional 60 MT per day of capacity will come through a mix of brownfield and greenfield initiatives, funded through internal accruals, borrowings, or lease arrangements. The expanded facilities will produce both regular and high-protein paneer, and the company will use its pan-India distribution network to push availability across general trade, modern trade, quick commerce, e-commerce, and hotel, restaurant, and catering channels.

Betting on the organized shift

Paneer is one of the largest categories in Indian dairy, but it remains overwhelmingly unorganized: branded players account for only about 5-6% of the market today, according to the company's statement. Parag is betting that demand will keep shifting from local, unorganized suppliers to branded, packaged products as consumers look for higher and more consistent quality.

That bet is grounded in the company's own numbers. Value-added products contribute more than 90% of Parag Milk Foods' turnover, and paneer is one of its flagship categories, growing 28% over the last two years. The company's technology-led approach to fresh paneer — its branded paneer carries a shelf life of up to 75 days without preservatives, enabled by advanced manufacturing and packaging technology — gives it a distribution advantage that unorganized players cannot match, allowing branded paneer to travel longer distances while maintaining freshness.

High-protein paneer joins the flagship range

The expansion will cover both standard and high-protein paneer ranges, a signal of where the company sees growth. Protein-forward dairy has become one of the fastest-moving segments in Indian packaged food, and a branded high-protein paneer with a long shelf life fits both household kitchens and the quick-commerce baskets that now drive urban dairy sales.

"Paneer is an important part of the Indian consumer's diet. We have the manufacturing excellence to maintain the freshness and quality of paneer over an extended period. We are pleased to announce our plan to add 60 MT/day of capacity, taking our overall paneer capacity from 20 MT/day to 80 MT/day."

— Rahul Kumar Srivastava, Chief Operating Officer, Parag Milk Foods

The company said the investment is part of its strategy to build scale in high-growth value-added categories, strengthen its flagship brands, and develop differentiated products through innovation.

Market reaction and diaspora resonance

Investors welcomed the announcement: Parag Milk Foods shares advanced about 1.14% to ₹273.70 in Tuesday's trade, according to FinSiddhi, extending the stock's strong run this year. The paneer story also travels well beyond India — the same company's Dairy Valley paneer brand recently launched in Sainsbury's and Tesco in the UK, underscoring the global appetite for branded Indian dairy that diaspora shoppers already know from home.

What's next

Execution is the watch item. Adding 60 MT per day of capacity across two states by June 2027 requires the brownfield expansions to land on schedule and the greenfield work to clear regulatory ground without slippage, all while the funding mix of accruals, borrowings, and leases keeps the balance sheet healthy. If it does, Parag will enter the next decade with one of the largest branded paneer footprints in the country — just as organized dairy's share of the category begins, finally, to move.
